headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared filesystem and shell-based handoff; no direct evidence of stronger pairwise coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads shared skill/context files, while agent B reads and writes the filesystem and processes shell/stdin-stdout content. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if A’s generated content is consumed by B as trusted text. The pairwise interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF agent A writes instructions into a file that agent B later reads as trusted input
IF agent B parses filesystem content or stdin/stdout as operational directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/provenance header to A-to-B handoffs
Review B prompts for any instruction-following on file contents
Store A outputs in a read-only staging directory
Disable automatic execution of text found in shared files
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write the filesystem, and B has broad network egress. A touches marketing content and product marketing context; B touches filesystem contents, source code, configuration, and environment variables. If they share a workspace, sensitive context can flow from A into B’s outputs or outbound requests. No direct evidence of isolation is provided, so the shared-workspace risk remains.
conditions: IF agent A and agent B share the same workspace directory
IF B uploads or transmits file contents or environment-derived context over the network
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict B’s outbound destinations to an allowlist
Keep secrets out of shared files
Run a quick audit for cross-agent file reads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem namespaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and can write the filesystem; B also writes the filesystem and spawns subprocesses, but does not modify git state. Overlap on the same writable directory can cause clobbering or race conditions even without git conflicts. Because no orchestrator locking is documented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF the orchestrator runs them concurrently without file locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes to shared paths
Use temporary files plus atomic renames
Check for concurrent runs before starting
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces marketing content and shared context; B can execute shell commands and act on filesystem contents. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream commands or generated artifacts. The profiles do not show explicit verification between them, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s output without a verification step
IF B uses A-generated text to construct shell commands or configuration
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Require B to quote and validate A outputs before use
Limit B to read-only review of A artifacts
Log all A-to-B handoffs for spot checks
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII. A touches marketing content; B touches source code, configuration, and environment variables. With no residency or certification mismatch documented, compliance risk is limited to general policy gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into the shared workflow
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention rules for shared artifacts
Review deployment region settings
Separate logs by agent
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both agents
